question: Which finding does the author use to support the claim that "distraction helps only when people do not notice they are being distracted"?

options.A: Patients rated their waits as longer after a television was added to a clinic waiting room.
options.B: Complaints at the post office fell after a screen showing estimated waits was put in place.
options.C: Customers told to expect ten minutes who then waited fifteen felt specifically cheated.
options.D: Customers rated waits in a single line as shorter even when the clock said otherwise.

question: Which detail from the passage most directly supports the idea that weighing still required careful attention?

options.A: Lise weighed a whole drawer of brass wood screws in under two minutes.
options.B: Bram spot-checked every drawer he weighed, sampling it from two corners.
options.C: Bram distrusted figures that he had not arrived at by himself.
options.D: The weight of each empty drawer was written in pencil on its side.

question: The author mentions the student who keeps a "public book" and a "real" sketchbook primarily to:

options.A: suggest that inexpensive paper produces better drawings than costly sketchbooks do.
options.B: show that many of the author's students have stopped keeping sketchbooks altogether.
options.C: contrast the author's students with the European painters described in paragraph 2.
options.D: illustrate how the pressure to share pages can push actual thinking somewhere private.

question: The author of Passage A would most likely agree that a heavy coat of moss on a tree's trunk:

options.A: is the main reason a growing trunk splits into furrows.
options.B: does no harm as long as no vine reaches the tree's crown.
options.C: can harm the tree by keeping water against its bark.
options.D: helps a tree that keeps its bark survive dry seasons.
